title: Effectiveness of a Generate–Verify–Repair Pipeline with Batfish for LLM‑Generated Vendor CLI Configurations
abstract: We report a preregistered paired experiment (cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1) that evaluated whether a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline—shared initial LLM candidate (gpt-5-mini) + a deterministic Batfish‑style validator + at most one automated LLM repair—reduces deterministic‑verifier detected semantic/safety failures on intent→vendor‑CLI tasks. Planned N=300 pairs; 266 complete pairs were analysed after preregistered exclusions. Baseline pass-rate = 260/266 (97.744%); guarded (final GVR) pass-rate = 265/266 (99.624%). Paired difference = 0.01879699248; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625. Paired bootstrap (B=10,000, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601]. Repair was invoked for 6 tasks; median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not recorded in per‑task artifacts and thus could not be evaluated. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the observed absolute improvement is small and did not meet the preregistered α=0.05 decision rule. We present preregistered design details, deterministic validator semantics, complete numeric outcomes, representative artifact‑grounded repair examples, contamination findings (no exact public duplicates flagged), and an evidence‑grounded discussion of limitations and implications.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being actively investigated for NetOps tasks such as intent→CLI translation, zero‑touch configuration synthesis, and automated maintenance workflows [1,2]. Because LLM outputs are stochastic, single‑shot generations can omit required commands, violate sequencing constraints, or touch protected fields—errors that deterministic network validators can detect and that, if applied to devices, could cause outages. Generate–verify–repair (GVR) architectures interpose deterministic verifiers (e.g., Batfish‑style validators) and permit bounded automated repairs to produce outputs that satisfy validator constraints before application [3,4]. Prior work has proposed components and small prototypes, but preregistered, paired evaluations with archived deterministic traces are limited.

Motivated by this gap, we preregistered and executed cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 to answer: Does a GVR pipeline that uses a single sampled initial LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate semantics), a deterministic Batfish‑style validator, and at most one automated LLM repair call reduce verifier‑detected semantic/safety failures relative to the same initial candidate without repair? Our principal contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired evaluation (Nplanned=300) executed under the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher constraints that reports exact paired contingency counts, the preregistered exact McNemar test, paired bootstrap interval estimates, execution accounting, representative artifact examples, and an evidence‑grounded discussion of validity threats specific to shared_initial_candidate semantics.
sections.related_work:
LLM applications in NetOps include intent→CLI translation systems and benchmarks that study automated configuration synthesis and correctness; NetConfEval and related studies evaluate whether LLMs can produce syntactically plausible configurations and discuss vendor‑syntax difficulties [1]. Surveys and tutorials summarize LLM failure modes in domain‑constrained tasks and recommend grounding and verifier augmentation when moving toward automation [2]. Generate–verify–repair architectures have been proposed in code generation and regulated domains to achieve deterministic validation via external oracles and bounded repair loops [3]. Network verification tools such as Batfish and header‑space analyses provide deterministic reachability and ordering checks and have been proposed as verifiers in LLM‑augmented NetOps prototypes [4]. Studies examining what LLMs require to synthesize correct router configurations emphasize sequencing and vendor‑syntax difficulties, motivating verifier augmentation [5].

Our work differs by (a) preregistering a paired estimand under shared_initial_candidate semantics so the comparison isolates validator‑triggered repair for a fixed initial candidate, (b) archiving raw model traces and deterministic validator traces for auditability, and (c) reporting exact paired counts and both exact and bootstrap inferential perspectives consistent with the preregistered analysis plan.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study preregistration is cnsms2026-001-gvr-batfish-prereg-v1 (manifest SHA‑256: 46a223492f760950b3d06f475129ce21e52e296c4c2a1e09df3ccd50bec9f891). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline under shared_initial_candidate semantics: the same single sampled initial model candidate is used to compute both the baseline outcome (single‑shot candidate → deterministic validator pass/fail) and the guarded outcome (same candidate → validator; if it fails, at most one automated LLM repair is permitted; final validator pass/fail recorded). This design isolates the marginal effect of the permitted automated repair on a fixed initial candidate.

Task bank and sampling: The preregistered task bank deterministically produced 300 intent→CLI pairs (150 Cisco‑like, 150 Juniper‑like) using a seeded synthetic task generator combined with public NetConfEval‑style examples; per‑task manifests, seeds, and generator identifiers are archived. Inclusion/exclusion, retry, and missingness rules followed the preregistration. Deterministic exclusion logic removed 34 both‑arm provider/infrastructure failures (analysis/missingness_summary.csv), leaving 266 complete paired units for the primary analysis.

Model and orchestration: Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json: declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini"). Archived model configuration fields include max_output_tokens=1024 and maximum_attempts_per_call=1; execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset) and no deterministic sampling seed, so nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded for the recorded provider calls. Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Provider call accounting (deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 306, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 272, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 34, and stage_counts recording shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 6.

Deterministic validator: The binary oracle used was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The validator performs CLI syntactic parsing/normalization, per‑task required‑sequence checks (expected_sequence vs parsed commands), allowed‑field touch checks, and reachability/constraint checks on the synthetic topology model. Each episode archives validation_before and validation_after traces including parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation codes, and normalized_configuration. The validator’s boolean pass/fail is the primary endpoint and is archived per episode under execution/scoring/*.json.

Repair loop and shared_initial_candidate mechanics: Per the preregistration the shared initial candidate is used by both arms. If the validator fails that candidate the guarded arm may invoke at most one automated LLM repair call. The repair prompt exposes the validator’s failure codes and task constraints and requests a corrected configuration; repair prompts and provider traces are archived when invoked. The ≤1 repair design was chosen to model a bounded automated correction before escalation/human review.

Analysis plan: The preregistered primary confirmatory test is the exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes (α=0.05). For interval estimation we preregistered a paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729). Missingness followed the preregistered complete_pair_primary rule: 34 both‑arm provider failures were excluded from the primary analysis; sensitivity analyses treat missing episodes conservatively as failures. Secondary estimands included median_repair_iterations_per_task and median end‑to‑end latency (latency could not be evaluated because per‑episode timing was not recorded). All analysis was executed by paired_binary_analysis_v1 and logged (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and missingness: Planned episodes = 600 (300 pairs × 2); completed episodes = 532; failed episodes = 68. Complete paired units analysed = 266; both_missing_pairs = 34 were excluded per preregistration (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Provider call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json): hosted_model_call_event_count = 306, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 272, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 34, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 272. Repair stage calls recorded = 6.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 266): baseline successes = 260; guarded final successes = 265. Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 260, n10 = 5, n01 = 0, n00 = 1. Observed proportions: baseline = 260/266 = 0.9774436090; guarded = 265/266 = 0.9962406015. Paired difference = 0.01879699248. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.0625 (preregistered α=0.05 decision rule → not significant). Paired bootstrap percentile CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) = [0.0037593984962406013, 0.03759398496240601] (analysis_log.jsonl documents seed and resample count).

Repair behavior and representative artifacts: Automated repair was invoked 6 times across 300 tasks; median repair iterations per task = 0. Representative example: task‑000008 shared initial candidate (execution/responses/task-000008-shared-initial.txt, sha256 = 89306095...) contained an incomplete trailing line and failed the validator (validation_before showed parsed_command_count mismatch). The guarded final artifact (execution/responses/task-000008-guarded.txt, sha256 = d52b7616f...) contains a corrected complete sequence; its validator trace indicates validation_after valid and lists the specific violation codes that triggered repair. All per‑episode validator traces and scoring decisions are archived in execution/scoring/*.json and the representative artifacts in the manuscript evidence bundle.

Contamination and sensitivity checks: analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty—no exact public‑duplicate tasks were flagged; hence no primary exclusions for contamination. Sensitivity analysis treating the 34 excluded both‑arm episodes as failures (conservative N=300 analysis) yields baseline = 260/300 = 0.866667 and guarded = 265/300 = 0.883333 with the same discordant counts (n10=5, n01=0) and exact McNemar p = 0.0625, confirming the primary inferential conclusion is stable under the preregistered conservative missingness handling.

Supplementary archived artifacts: condition_summary.csv and paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 hashed) are available in analysis artifacts; deterministic_reconciliation.json documents that all deterministic consistency checks passed and provides provider call and stage counts used above.
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation: The guarded GVR pipeline produced a small absolute increase in validator pass‑rate (~1.88 percentage points). Under the preregistered exact McNemar decision rule the improvement did not reach α=0.05 (p=0.0625). The paired bootstrap CI excludes zero while the exact McNemar test does not; this arises because McNemar’s exact test depends only on discordant counts (here n10=5, n01=0) and yields discrete p‑values, whereas the bootstrap CI summarizes empirical paired‑difference variability across resamples (B=10,000, seed=1729). Reporting both perspectives makes explicit the finite‑sample inferential nuance.

Operational implications and boundary conditions: The limited marginal benefit of the bounded automated repair is largely explained by the high baseline single‑shot pass rate (≈97.7%), leaving few failures for repair to correct; repair was invoked only 6 times. For workloads with lower first‑pass accuracy, or when validator coverage expands to detect more failure classes, GVR’s marginal benefit may be larger. We do not claim production readiness: results apply to the tested synthetic/public task corpus and the specific validator rule battery.

Threats to validity: Internal validity—shared_initial_candidate semantics measure the effect of validator‑triggered repair for a fixed initial sample and do not evaluate independent multiple draws or constrained first‑pass prompting (such arms were not executed per the preregistration). Construct validity—the deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite set of syntactic/sequence/reachability rules; semantic violations outside this battery are unmeasured. External validity—tasks come from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor dialect clusters; results may not generalize to other vendors, larger topologies, or production networks. Conclusion validity—few discordant pairs and the exclusion of 34 provider‑failure pairs reduced precision; future studies should plan for larger N if baseline pass rates are expected to be high.

Design lessons: (1) When baseline pass rates are high, evaluate repair effectiveness on lower‑baseline corpora or broaden validator coverage. (2) Archive per‑episode latency to permit operational latency bounds (the preregistered latency endpoint could not be evaluated because timing was not recorded). (3) Expand validator rule batteries and measure verifier false negatives as part of construct‑validity assessment. (4) Consider separate preregistered arms for independent multi‑draw generation or constrained prompting to measure other mitigation strategies explicitly.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a preregistered paired experiment testing a GVR pipeline (gpt‑5‑mini initial candidate + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + ≤1 automated repair) on intent→CLI tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Across 266 analysed pairs the guarded pipeline improved validator pass‑rate by 0.01879699248 but did not meet the preregistered exact‑McNemar α=0.05 decision rule (p=0.0625); a paired bootstrap CI (B=10,000, seed=1729) narrowly excludes zero. Repair calls were rare (6/300) and median repair iterations per task = 0. Per‑episode latency was not archived and could not be assessed. All execution and analysis artifacts, including raw responses, validator traces, provider call accounting, and reconciliation manifests, are archived in the evidence bundle to support reanalysis and follow‑on work.

[1] C. Wang, M. Scazzariello, A. Farshin, S. Ferlin, D. Kostić, and M. Chiesa, “NetConfEval: Can LLMs Facilitate Network Configuration?,” in Proc. ACM, 2024. DOI: 10.1145/3656296.
[2] S. Y. Long et al., “A Survey on Intelligent Network Operations and Performance Optimization Based on Large Language Models,” IEEE Commun. Surveys & Tutorials, 2025. DOI: 10.1109/COMST.2025.3526606.
[3] R. Cadenas, “Convergent Correctness in Stochastic Code Generation: A Generate‑Verify‑Repair Architecture for Deterministic Validation of Autonomous AI Coding Agents in Regulated Environments,” SSRN, 2026. DOI: 10.2139/ssrn.6754899.
[4] M. Brown, A. Fogel, D. Halperin, V. Heorhiadi, R. Mahajan, and T. Millstein, “Lessons from the evolution of the Batfish configuration analysis tool,” Proc., 2023. DOI: 10.1145/3603269.3604866.
[5] R. Mondal, A. Tang, R. Beckett, T. Millstein, and G. Varghese, “What do LLMs need to Synthesize Correct Router Configurations?,” Proc., 2023. DOI: 10.1145/3626111.3628194.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: both arms used the same single sampled initial candidate per preregistration; the estimand measures validator‑triggered repair benefit for that fixed initial sample and does not evaluate independent first‑pass generations or constrained first‑pass prompting strategies.

Missingness and sample reduction: planned N=300 pairs; after infrastructure/provider exclusions 266 pairs were complete and 34 both‑arm episodes were excluded per preregistered rules, reducing effective sample size and precision.
Small discordant counts: primary inference used exact McNemar with few discordants (n10=5, n01=0); conclusions are sensitive to inferential choice and limited power.
Validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a finite set of syntactic/semantic/reachability rules; semantic violations outside its coverage are possible and unmeasured.
Runtime nondeterminism and sampling: execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null and no deterministic seed; nondeterministic sampling cannot be excluded for recorded model calls.
H2 latency not evaluated: per‑episode end‑to‑end latency was not present in archived per‑task artifacts and therefore the preregistered latency bound (median ≤ 60 s) could not be assessed.

External validity: task corpus derives from public NetConfEval‑style examples and a seeded synthetic generator limited to two vendor‑dialect clusters; results do not imply universal benefit across other vendors, larger topologies, or production deployments.
